text: Big store. Super clean. Super friendly staff. Low stock of Meji Greek style yoghurt in the 1000g tubs.

This  REVIEW  is about the Gold Shop on the second floor. I went there with my wife a couple weeks ago to look at gold necklaces. Two gold shops and both had good displays of bracelets and babbles. the lowest price range was One thousand bahts. I did not understand the price symbols. But the bored workers there let us look at a few pieces and it became apparent that the price 10,000 baht plus. Then next lowest category was 20,000 +. think we were the only customers there.The necklace that my wife liked was 19,500 baht. I did not want to pay that much but felt shamed by the contempt that the workers showed me and was kind of manipulated into agreeing to buy it to not lose face. The guy refused to accept my visa card. So I walked to the ATM and withdrew 20,000 baht and paid cash. They made a big big deal out the transaction, insisting on making a photocopy of my Passport like these people are so fond of doing... No courtesy - just took  my money and handed over the piece with the receipt.... today we went back there because the thin gold chain had broken.  Wan still had the receipt and she said maybe they would charge her something to make the repair so I gave her 2,000 baht and I went there with her... two women working there and again no customers. The young woman wai'd to us and my wife showed her the broken necklace and receipt. She weighed the piece for some reason and then another woman came into the shop. the other one patted her down. i.e. she felt her bra, front and back, under the bra strap and her hips and waist. Then this one - ignoring me - again weighed the piece and took out the pieces that Wan was considering. The trip was they would exchange the broken chain for a new necklace. I mentioned that she wanted one with a thicker, stronger chain. So the skinny woman who had been searched wrote out a receipt showing a cost of 1,740 baht for the service. I tried to object that if it was under warranty and being exchanged  we should not have to pay. Wan told me that they said she was not supposed to sleep with the necklace on so they would not honor the warranty.
Fine.
We got the new necklace and I helped fasten the clasp and then Wan gave her 2,000 baht. Then they made us wait and wait and wait and wait.... They of course whipped out the cell phone and punched in numbers and showed us that they would give us 260 baht in change. I am old enough to have learned how to count. Then they had to punch the numbers on their computer and print out some more papers. and Wan had to sign some more copies and then they went back to being bored. and we sat and waited and waited and got fed up and walked to the counter and asked the skinny woman what was the problem. I spoke into the TRANSLATE app on my cell phone and showed it to her. and also I told her in Thai and English that she was wasting our time ,. she ignored me and spoke  gibberish to Wan and went back and punched more numbers on the computer and ignored me. Finally she showed Wan two copies of receipts and had her sign them in two places and tore off the bottom part of each paper and then she went back to her computer and then consulted with the co-worker and then counted out the two thousand bahts and then counted out the 260 in change.
I would have left the 260 baht there if I had known they were going to make us wait and wait so long. No wai, no courtesy, no respect. I have read reviews of other gold shops in Chiang Mai where the customers said the owners were very nice. But at this Lotus Ruamchok they are contemptuous.

Great little mall. Can do everything here. Restaurants, mobile sim cards, pay bills, get amazing peanut covers donuts at Mr. Donut. There is a full food court and other stores on the lower level and a MR DYI and lotus upstairs. you can get most anything you need as far as grocery stores go. If lotus don't have it go across the street to Rimping Market or Topps.

Well, it's not the cheapest supermarket in Chiang Mai, but at least you can find almost everything here. The whole mall is pleasant, you will find restaurants, food court, bakery, clothing stores before entering the supermarket.
Good place to do your groceries shopping.  Big supermarket. Free parking. Some restaurants and foods court  available inside the mall.

One of KFC friendchise located in Tesco Lotus (RuamChok). The restaurant is well decorated .Their fried chicken is delicious. Other than fried chicken you can also order hamburger , rice with friedchicken or fish and dessert. You can park in Tesco Lotus (RuamChok) parking lot.
Good quality food and good prices. Staff are very friendly and helpful.
This is a nice store which was a bit far from the Huaykaew road where I was staying. It sells fresh produce, groceries, water, electronics, house hold items at great prices.
Quiet in the mornings and a lot more things on sale in the produce section early--but not on the weekend.

Was looking for ground beef for hamburgers and meatballs. Beef and pork are the two main kinds of meat. This Lotus only sells pork. They don't sell beef or ground (minced) beef. Extremely strange, especially for such a big supermarket. That's like going to a supermarket and trying to buy water but they don't sell water. A supermarket chain that doesn't sell beef or ground beef. Don't waste your time at these supermarkets that don't sell the necessities. Go to Big C or Makro

Lotus's is a great department store consisting of food on one side, clothing and personal items in the middle,  and white goods and household items on the far side that is right next to a Mr DIY.
(Another shop I love going into).

Meats are fresh and vege are almost organic. The price are more reasonable than any other groceries in the neighbourhood. Moreover, the staff are friendly and very helpful. Although it has lots of outdoor parkings, the indoor parking lots are very limited.

I just had my dinner at the food court and after that shopped at mr. DIY.
Did not go to Lotus which in itself is an OK shop, it is unfortunate that the staff that works in small bakery don't seem to be able to make sure that the prices of products they sell are never there where the products are.
But, when asked someone will help you.

Classic big Lotus supermarket with the exact same layout as the other ones. Same shops. However the food court has only a few options, and looks quite dreary (like most food courts in a mall).

No proper cafes, there is Miracle coffee with two small tables (mostly for takeaway), and a two others at the food court.

There is a BATA shoe shop downstairs.

Mr DIY next to the supermarket is a great addition. With them together, you can find almost anything you need.

There is a massage shop upstairs where the employees are senior citizens- a nice initiative.

The entire place is uncomfortably lit up with bright white lights, not an issue for most people.

Open since 8 AM is great for all early bird. Bare in mind that other shop inside Lotus is still close at 8AM.
There is Mr.DIY inside this store which is a great place to get your general household items, tools, etc.

The meat and fish has been and disappointment. The fish is not fresh the chicken was also old with bad smell, the beef only frozen old and very expensive. The store also lacks the product selection that are available at other Tesco. Despite this is the closest location to my home I am not coming again. No Halal meat products at all

This is a downscale mini mall that I used only because it is convenient for paying my mobile phone bill. The fact that it has just had a second Covid cluster within its building this year speaks volumes about the token effort it puts into maintaining a safe environment. I will not be returning.

This is a smallish version of this popular chain in Thailand. Technically, you have all you need here. The supermarket, a food court, ATM, fast food, etc. There's a IT store here as well. I did say it was a smallish version. Sometimes, the items you want may not be in stock.

Better  bakery choice, than in south Tesco.
Evening discount near 7 PM :)
Good coverage of product range in the supermarket. Doesn't have a lot of proper restaurant choices. The food court is so and so. Plenty of parking space though.
Great selection and low prices. Good axillary service too. I got shopping done and bought some hardware at DIY and got a foot massage all while getting an oil change 😁 …

Typical Tesco Lotus, that is very loud music from different parts of the store, all different. Sounds like a nightclub. Have no idea how this even happens. Do they think it sells more stuff??? Also, the staff don't have a clue about the products, and pretty much mill about hoping you won't ask questions, even in Thai. Try to get a straight answer about anything that is out of stock, forget it. Store layout ridiculous as most people are in about four spots and the rest is a no man's land of meters of space everyone has to walk through. Only good if you want some cheap small appliance. For everything else, stay away.

One of two chains of modern grocery stores located throughout Thailand carrying many typically Western items.  Prices for produce and meats are not as reasonable as local markets but quality can be higher and certainly more hygienic.

This is a large Tesco in the common top-floor supermarket layout with a variety of other shops on the ground floor.

The supermarket product selection is reasonably good but has a poor fresh produce section compared to the khamtieng branch.

Never gets old.

A great variety of shops;restaurants,cafes and parking.
One of our 'go to' places in CM
Visited it for buying groceries and also found a playground for kids that is good and fun enough for toddler riding carousel.

Tesco Lotus is a good spot for picking up the essentials. (For more variety or specialty items, we would recommend Rimping, Tops, or Big-C - otherwise, this is a great option.)

Parking usually isn't a problem, and there is a KFC, MK Suki, a few other dining options, Dairy Queen, S&P Bakery, and a Watsons(?). Also the B-Quik and carwash place makes this location quite convenient and popular.
OK,  nice store, but you need to stick American food such as, Boston Market frozen dinners,  Quaker Oatmeal in a box packet.  For foreign customers.
Typical supermarket, but I would recommend spicy fish salad roll and dimsum at food court entrance on ground floor. They deserve 5 star rating.
Good cheap staples. Clothing, and household bric a brac. More oriented to local shoppers, but a good solid hypermarket chain.
Good supermarket to visit. Friendly customer services.  Good range of fresh and dry foods to serve.
You can find everything there and it's really cheap. Lot of fruits and vegetables, fresh meat and fishes. Also a little food court. Great place to eat or take away.
Good for parking, a decent selection of food and non food goods although I found the breads / bakery section lacking. Pretty good for a supermarket.
Nice place chill and relax for a bit. A lot of food options. Good Thai food also. Upper floor has groceries and such.
There's a wide variety of different article's to buy. Food and nonfood. And many things for household and kichen.
Very well stocked supermarket with many many other outlets available. Ample carpark
an excellent shopping experience nice and clean surroundings family oriented. happy to see you nice manageable Mall thank you.
Nice shopping place
Giving a sale on a regular basis. Not crowded. Can find discount items often.
All Tesco Lotus are basically the same, so I will go to them occasionally because I know what to expect. This one is on one of my bike riding routes in Chiang Mai, so I have been there a few times.
